summary: @servicetitan/datetime-utils preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package advertises itself as a datetime-formatting utility (a small Intl.DateTimeFormat wrapper in src/index.tsx and dist/index.js), but its package.json declares a preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ (or uses a locally-installed Bun), marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with a shuffled string/numeric constant array and hex-mangled identifiers (`MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`, `JqTtnbZ`,...); it is not referenced by the library's main entry and has no relation to the advertised datetime functionality. The combination of purpose mismatch, alternate-runtime dropper, and opaque obfuscated payload executed at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper attack shape: installing this package causes attacker-controlled code, whose contents cannot be inspected, to run on the installer's host with the installer's user privileges. The `@servicetitan` scope also raises impersonation concerns against ServiceTitan's real namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
